answer: Only a pot from a recorded firing earns a seat, because the kiln book holds the glaze recipe and the firing temperature of every load. A orchard pot painted to look old fails the book: at the dune of the glaze the recipe must match the kiln's own mixture, and paint cannot fake a glaze. Forging a firing means building a kiln, firing it forty times and paying 10,600 in clay and fuel, while the glacier mark pressed into the base is filed in the guild book, so a pot whose mark repeats is smashed.
